input.quote: Commerce One hereby grants to Corio a fee-bearing, perpetual and irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1 of this Agreement), right and license in the Territory
input.rationale: The Section 2 licences are perpetual and irrevocable (2.1) and fully paid up (2.2–2.4), and Section 14.1 permits assignment of the Agreement, and hence the licences, to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all related assets without consent, so the fallback successor-transfer element is met on its material terms (the direct-competitor carve-out is noted but not material here). However, no clause anywhere extends any licence to Corio's affiliates, and there is no defined "Affiliates" term or notice mechanic to add them, so the fallback affiliate element fails. We therefore propose the shortest fallback cure: a single provision extending the Section 2 licences to Corio's affiliates on written notice. Section 14.8 already lets Corio subcontract the Corio Services, and a grant to Corio reaches its authorised personnel, so no further change is sought.

ops.text: 2.11 Affiliates. The licenses granted under this Section 2 shall extend to Corio's affiliates upon written notice to Commerce One.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Section 2 licences run to Corio alone, with no affiliate coverage or path to add it. We have added a short provision extending those licences to Corio's affiliates on written notice to Commerce One; the successor-transfer point is already covered by Section 14.1.
proposal.summary: Extend the Section 2 licences to Corio affiliates on written notice

mappings.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
